name: Bimal Krishna Matilal
shortBio: Indian analytic philosopher and Sanskritist who brought classical Nyaya-Vaisesika logic, epistemological realism, and Buddhist pramana debates into direct dialogue with contemporary Western philosophy of language.
centralQuestion: How do classical Nyaya theories of perception, inference, and epistemic warrant solve problems of reference and skepticism in modern analytic philosophy?

keyWorks.title: Perception: An Essay on Classical Indian Theories of Knowledge
keyWorks.description: Landmark analytical defense of Nyaya direct realism against Buddhist phenomenalism and Western sense-datum theories.

keyWorks.title: The Character of Logic in India
keyWorks.description: Demonstrates the formal rigor of non-deductive, debate-centered Indian inference (anumana) and Dignaga’s logic.
